seen_animation: A head-only doodle cat sits to the right of a grey triangular hill shape. In frames 1-6 the head is turned toward the viewer's right: the eyes, nose, mouth and right-side whiskers are packed against the right edge of the outline, only the right ear stands up clearly, and the left side of the head is a plain rounded contour with two left whiskers. The pose barely changes across frames 1-6. In frame 7 the head has turned most of the way to face the viewer: both ears are up, the features sit slightly right of center. From frame 8 to 16 the head is fully frontal with features centered, matching the doodle, and stays still with only very small shifts in outline and whisker position.
seen_film: A reclining tiger lies on a rock with its body stretched to the lower left and forelegs to the lower right; its head is at the top center-right of the frame. In frames 1-6 the head is turned toward the viewer's right and slightly down, holding nearly still. Between frames 6 and 7 the tiger turns its head to look straight at the camera; frame 7 is already close to frontal with both ears visible. Frames 8-16 hold the frontal stare with only small head movements. The body does not move.
named_subject: A doodled cat face standing in for the tiger's head (head only, no body).
evidence: Frames 1-6 of both show the head turned to the viewer's right and held; both turn to frontal between frames 6 and 7 (animation frame 7 is an in-between with features still slightly right, film frame 7 is near frontal); frames 8-16 of both hold a frontal stare. The head is placed in the upper center-right of the frame in both, at roughly the same horizontal position. Frames 8-16 of the animation match c.png nearly stroke for stroke (ear shapes, crossed brow stroke, tick eyes, open nose shape, J-shaped mouth, long right whisker crossing the outline).
primary_gap: The turned-away drawing in frames 1-6 squeezes the eyes, nose, mouth and whiskers into a tangle against the right edge of the outline, so the three-quarter pose reads less clearly than the frontal pose and the left ear is missing rather than foreshortened.
closes_when: In frames 1-6 the features are shifted right but keep their spacing and the doodle's stroke shapes, with a small left ear tip still visible behind the head, so the frame 6 to 8 change reads as the same face rotating.
protect: The timing of the turn between frames 6 and 7 with an in-between at frame 7; the head's position in the frame; the frontal frames 8-16 that reproduce c.png's construction and stroke habits; the near-stillness of the holds, matching the film's still tiger; the plain open-stroke style without added detail.
identity_gap: The frontal frames are clearly the doodle, but in frames 1-6 the turned face's features overlap and lose the doodle's clear separate strokes, and the left ear is dropped.
